newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ SPORT - NZRFU moves to secure player contracts.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT - NZRFU moves to secure player contracts.

text.p: WELLINGTON, Oct 21 - Rugby administrators are moving swiftly to avoid a major threat from Northern Hemisphere clubs targeting New Zealand players with big money, NZPA reported on Monday.

New Zealand Rugby Football Union (NZRFU) chief executive officer David Moffett said the union was aware of the northern attraction, but there was no danger of New Zealand losing any current All Black at this stage.
He said the union was moving quickly to extend the All Blacks' contracts or secure further contracts at the end of those expiring in the near future.
As much attention was directed towards securing younger players, he said.

Stuard Gallagher, chairman of Welsh Club Llanelli, has warned New Zealand that British clubs were switching their focus on younger New Zealand players after finding difficulties luring All Blacks and high-profile players because of their existing provincial, Super 12 or NZRFU contracts.

He said it was strange that All Blacks Robin and Zinzan Brooke and Michael Jones were associated with leading English sides Harlequins, Bath and Northampton as their contracts with the NZRFU ran into next season.
"They can't go and play there without our consent," Moffett said today.
"Even a lot of younger players are contracted through the (rugby) academy or by way of the Super 12 but we are moving to secure them as well.
"There is a fair bit of movement but it's no more than what we've had in the past. A lot of players are going there (Northern Hemisphere) but not the high profile ones.
"It seems England cannot develop its own players and is looking at countries like us, Australia and South Africa to try and get their ranks filled.
"We'll be cautioning our younger players because we're not sure just how long that sort of money is going to last in the Northern Hemisphere.
"All these clubs are backed by businessmen who want a return for their investment.
"But suffice to say that we have a plan, which is confidential, to protect our resource which is the players.
"At the end of the day we have a policy that if you want to play for the All Blacks you have to live and play in this country -- that is something the UK cannot offer the younger players."
English champions Bath reportedly mounted a bid for All Black lock Robin Brooke.

It followed, according to reports, Brooke turning down a Stg100,000 ($NZ228,000) offer from Northampton, coached by British Lions mentor Ian McGeechan. The club lifted their offer to Stg150,000 after greeting card tycoon Andrew Brownsword injected a Stg2.5 million sponsorship for the club.
Former All Blacks Va'aiga Tuigamala and Frano Botica have been snatched up by British rugby clubs in the league off-season.
